_about: Sourced geometry fixes to the border data before 1992, applied by tools/build_patches.py after tools/build_clio.py. Each patch says what was wrong and how it is fixed; the operations are described in the tool's header. Fixes that only rename, hide or clip a shape belong in content/corrections.json instead.

patches.note: Cliopatria draws Czechoslovakia inside the Soviet Union in 1969-1990, the years Soviet troops were stationed there after the 1968 invasion, and parts of Afghanistan as Soviet territory in 1979-1989. Czechoslovakia remained a separate state, and Afghanistan was ruled by its own communist government. The Soviet Union's frontiers did not change between 1953 and Lithuania's declaration of independence in 1990, so its 1953-1968 outline is used for 1969-1989 and its 1991 outline for 1990.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia

patches.note: From 1949 to 1990 East Berlin was the capital of the German Democratic Republic and West Berlin a separate city tied to the Federal Republic, under the Western Allies. The border data draws East Berlin as part of the Soviet Union, the American, British and French sectors of West Berlin as parts of those countries, all of Berlin as East German in 1973-1975, and the city about 8 km north of where it is. West Berlin is redrawn from its boundary (Glienicke Bridge, Staaken, Spandau, Frohnau, the Wall at Bornholmer Straße, the Brandenburg Gate, Checkpoint Charlie and the Oberbaum Bridge, Rudow, Lichtenrade), cut out of the GDR, and East Berlin is part of the GDR.

Czechoslovakia was restored as a state in 1945 and existed until 31 December 1992. The border data leaves it out in 1945-1946 and 1969-1990, when it draws the country as Soviet; its 1953-1968 outline is used for those years. Soviet forces left in December 1945 and were stationed again from 1968 to 1991.

With the Soviet outline trimmed to the Soviet Union itself (soviet-union-outline), Afghanistan is drawn whole in 1979-1991, with the border data's own outline of 1976-1978, which fits the Soviet outline. Afghanistan's borders did not change. (That outline, like the border data's for every year from 1919, puts a strip north of the Amu Darya around Termez on the Afghan side.) The Democratic Republic of Afghanistan (from 1987 the Republic of Afghanistan) held Kabul and the main cities until April 1992; the war maps show the areas each side controlled.
Southern Yemen became independent on 30 November 1967; the border data has no state there in 1968.
Bangladesh became independent in December 1971; the border data has no state there in 1972.
Qatar became independent on 3 September 1971; the border data has no state there in 1972.
Bahrain became independent on 15 August 1971; the border data has no state there in 1972.
The Sultanate of Oman (so named after the 1970 coup) has no outline in the border data in 1972.
The United Arab Emirates were formed on 2 December 1971; the border data has no state there in 1972.
The Arab Federation of Iraq and Jordan ended in August 1958; the border data has no state in Jordan in 1959.
Cyprus became independent on 16 August 1960; the border data has no state there in 1960.
The Gambia became independent on 18 February 1965; the border data has no state there in 1965-1966.
Malawi became independent on 6 July 1964; the border data has no state there in 1965-1966.
Zambia became independent on 24 October 1964; the border data has no state there in 1965-1966.
Djibouti became independent on 27 June 1977; the border data has no state there in 1977-1978.
Algeria became independent on 5 July 1962; the border data has no state there in 1962.
Ghana became independent on 6 March 1957; the border data has no state there in 1957.
Libya became independent on 24 December 1951 after two years of UN-supervised transition from British and French administration; the border data has no state there in 1951-1952.
Fiji became independent on 10 October 1970; the border data has no state there in 1971-1972.
Grenada became independent on 7 February 1974; the border data draws it as a British colony until 1975.
Malta became independent on 21 September 1964; the border data draws it as British until 1966.
Singapore left Malaysia and became independent on 9 August 1965; the border data draws it inside Malaysia until 1966.
Brunei became independent on 1 January 1984; the border data draws it inside Malaysia until 1986.
Tanganyika and Zanzibar united as Tanzania on 26 April 1964; the border data leaves Zanzibar out of Tanzania until 1966. Tanzania's 1967 outline is used for 1965-1966.
A piece of Chukotka around Cape Dezhnev is drawn as part of the United States from the Alaska Purchase on; it was always Russian (then Soviet).
Two specks of the Republic of India lie far outside it, in southern Afghanistan (63.8E 29.5N) and near Quetta in Pakistan (66.3E 29.95N).
After Bangladesh's independence (1971) a speck of Pakistan is left on the Bangladesh coast (90.05E 22.0N).

The Comoros (independent 6 July 1975) are drawn as part of the Republic of Cabo Verde, an archipelago off West Africa. The Comoro islands are taken out of Cabo Verde and drawn as the Comoros, from Natural Earth, without Mayotte, which stayed French.
The Maldives became independent on 26 July 1965 (a British protectorate before); the border data never draws them.
Western Samoa became independent on 1 January 1962; the border data never draws it.
Tonga, a kingdom under British protection from 1900, regained full sovereignty on 4 June 1970; the border data never draws it.
Nauru became independent on 31 January 1968; the border data never draws it.
Tuvalu became independent on 1 October 1978; the border data never draws it.
Kiribati became independent on 12 July 1979; the border data never draws it.
The Marshall Islands became self-governing in free association with the United States on 21 October 1986; the border data never draws them.
Saint Kitts and Nevis became independent on 19 September 1983; the border data never draws it.
Vatican City became a sovereign state under the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929; the border data draws it as part of Italy.
San Marino's independence was recognised by the Papacy in 1631 and its borders have not changed since 1463; the border data draws it only in 1797-1799. Natural Earth's outline is used for 1631-1991.
Liechtenstein has been sovereign since 1806 within its 1719 borders; the border data draws it until 1814 and then as part of its neighbours. Natural Earth's outline is used for 1815-1991.

Monaco has had its present borders since the Franco-Monegasque Treaty of 1861. The border data has no Monaco from 1815 to 1944, and from 1945 draws it over Nice; Natural Earth's outline is used for 1861-1991.
The Bahamas (independent 10 July 1973) are drawn as a few misplaced blobs that miss New Providence and Nassau; Natural Earth's outline is used instead.

After Bahrain, Qatar and the Trucial States became independent in 1971, the United Kingdom's shape still contains them and Oman (the corrections layer hides these pieces, but the map put the United Kingdom's name there). The pieces are removed from 1972 on.

The Sultanate of Muscat and Oman (renamed the Sultanate of Oman in August 1970) was an independent state with close British ties, never a British colony or protectorate. The border data draws Muscat and Salalah as British from the 1920s and all of Oman as British from 1956 to 1971, merged with the Trucial States (British-protected, today's United Arab Emirates) and the Aden protectorates. Oman is drawn as its own state, with its 1973 outline from 1956, and the British shape keeps only the Trucial States and, until 1967, Aden. (In 1947-1955 the border data files Oman's outline under the name Qatar Protectorate, which the corrections layer shows as the Sultanate of Muscat and Oman.)

Malaysia's shape still contains Singapore after its separation on 9 August 1965, and a strip of Brunei until 1986; from 1984 it also lacks Limbang (part of Sarawak, so Malaysian since 1963). Malaysia's 1967 outline (without Singapore) is used for 1965-1966 and its 1987 outline (with Limbang, without Brunei) for 1984-1986.

From 261 to 429 the border data draws Roman Africa as a coastal strip and leaves inland Numidia and the two Mauretanias blank (Cirta, Sitifis, Lambaesis, Thamugadi, Altava), though these provinces stayed Roman until the Vandal conquest of the 430s: Diocletian split Numidia in two and made Mauretania Sitifensis a province in 293, Constantine renamed Cirta Constantina, and the frontier works (Fossatum Africae) date from Hadrian to Constantine and were abandoned in 430-440 after the Vandal invasion. The land the data's own 260 outline has and its 261 outline lacks, east of the Moulouya (2.4 W), is added to the Roman Empire (261-394) and the Western Roman Empire (395-429). Southern Mauretania Tingitana (Volubilis, given up c. 285) is not restored. In 337-346 the added piece overlaps the data's coastal strip by about 150 km2 along its inland edge.

Under Septimius Severus the African frontier moved south: Q. Anicius Faustus, legate of the Third Legion, built the forts of the Limes Tripolitanus at Gheriat el-Garbia and Bu Njem (Golaia) in 197-201, a Roman garrison held Castellum Dimmidi (Messaad) from about 198 to 240, and Gemellae had been a fort since Hadrian. The border data keeps the older line 1-2 degrees to the north, with all four outside. Two strips south of the data's own frontier are added to the Roman Empire: the Tripolitanian pre-desert from the Djebel Dahar (Tillibari) past Gheriat and Bu Njem to the Syrtic frontier, for 198-260 (the data's frontier is unchanged until 260), and a strip in pre-Saharan Algeria around Castellum Dimmidi and Gemellae, for 198-240. The southern edge is approximate, drawn a little beyond the forts; Ghadames (Cidamus) and the deep desert that the Ancient World Mapping Center shades are left out.

Darius I's first campaign in south-east Europe began in 513 BCE, and Thrace became the Persian satrapy of Skudra (re-subjugated by Mardonius in 492 BCE). Persian rule ended after Plataea (479 BCE), lingering at Doriscus until about 465 BCE. The border data draws Thrace as Persian only in 480-479 BCE. The satrapy is added to the Achaemenid Empire for 513-481 BCE, drawn from its described limits: the Macedonian kingdom (a vassal, drawn separately) and the Pirin and Rila ranges to about Kostenets in the west, the Haemus (Balkan) range in the north, and the Pontic coast to the Danube, with Dobruja. The Greek coastal cities the atlas draws on their own (Byzantium and Perinthus, the Pontic colonies, the Chersonese towns and the Aegean coast east of the Nestos) are left as they are. The inland boundary is approximate; the Danube plain west of Dobruja (Moesia), which some maps also shade, is left out.

Southern Gaul (Gallia Transalpina, later Narbonensis) became a Roman province in 121 BCE, after Q. Fabius Maximus defeated the Allobroges and the Arverni, and Narbo was founded in 118 BCE. The border data draws only a coastal corridor from 110 BCE and the province's interior (Tolosa, Nemausus, Carcaso, Vienna) as Roman only from 50 BCE. The land the data's 50 BCE outline adds over each year's outline, inside the province's limits (the Pyrenees, the Cevennes, Lake Geneva and the Alps, drawn as a simplified outline in two parts that keeps Lugdunum out), is added to the Roman Republic for 121-51 BCE. Massalia, an allied city until 49 BCE, stays outside, as in the data. The inland boundary is approximate.

Augustus granted Herod Trachonitis, Batanaea and Auranitis in 22 BCE; at Herod's death (4 BCE) they passed to his son Philip. The border data draws them as Roman and keeps Judea west of them. A box over Batanaea, Trachonitis and northern Auranitis (35.7-36.95 E, 32.62-33.33 N), less what Judea already has, is added to Judea for 22-4 BCE, and the corrections layer cuts the same box out of the Roman Empire in those years. The outline is a rectangle, so its edges are approximate.

Li Yuan proclaimed the Tang on 18 June 618, but the border data draws the whole Sui until 622 and starts the Tang in 623, and the map hides the Sui after 618, so China was blank in 619-622. The Tang took the rest of the country piece by piece: Liu Wuzhou in Shanxi (620), Wang Shichong at Luoyang and Dou Jiande in Hebei (621), Xiao Xian's Liang on the middle Yangtze (621), Li Zitong's Wu (621) and Lin Shihong's Chu in Jiangxi and Guangdong (622); Gao Kaidao held the far north of Hebei until 624. The data's first split of the Sui lands (623) is copied back to 619-622: the Tang outline for the Tang, Gao Kaidao's for Gao Kaidao, and the rest (the south, Hebei and Liang Shidu's Ordos) as the land of the rival regimes, which the map labels as such (content/corrections.json); the Eastern Göktürks take their 623 outline too, which leaves the Ordos out, so the two do not overlap. It is an approximation: in 619-620 the Tang did not yet hold Henan, and the rivals' land was divided among several states that are not drawn separately.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Transition from Sui to Tang

patches.note: The Tang ended on 1 June 907, when Emperor Ai abdicated to Zhu Wen (Later Liang), but the border data draws the Tang until 910 and starts its successor states only in 911, and the map hides the Tang after 907, so China was blank in 908-910. The states the data draws in 911 already existed: the Later Liang, Former Shu, Wuyue and Chu date from 907, Wu from 902-907, Li Maozhen's Qi at Fengxiang and Li Keyong's Jin at Taiyuan from the Tang's last years, Liu Shouguang held Youzhou (Yan) from 907, Wang Shenzhi became Prince of Min in 909, Liu Yin was governor at Guangzhou (later Southern Han) from 905, and Abaoji became khagan of the Khitan (later Liao) in 907. Each state's 911 outline is copied back to 908-910; the map's labels for 911 (Former Jin for the data's 'Later Jin', Liao for the Khitan) apply from 908.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period

patches.note: Zhu Yuanzhang proclaimed the Ming at Nanjing on 23 January 1368 and took the Yuan capital Dadu in September 1368; Toghon Temür fled to Shangdu and the Northern Yuan began. The border data starts the Ming only in 1375 and draws the whole Yuan, China proper included, until 1374, so the map showed China as Northern Yuan in 1369-1374. The Ming's 1375 outline is copied back to 1368-1374 and the Yuan rows of 1368-1374 take the Northern Yuan's 1375 outline (the steppe north of the Ming). Approximate: Sichuan (Ming Xia, to 1371), Gansu and Liaodong came over in 1369-1372, and Yunnan and Guizhou held out for the Yuan under Basalawarmi until 1381-82 (blank here, as in the data's 1375-1381 outlines).

The border data's Eastern Wu for 207-237 is only its lower-Yangtze core (about 0.6 million km²) and leaves southern Jing (Hunan) and Jiao Province (Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, northern Vietnam) to the Han, which the map hides after 223 so they were blank in 224-237. Sun Quan made Bu Zhi Inspector of Jiao Province in 210, gained Changsha and Guiyang in 215, and took the rest of Liu Bei's Jing Province in Lü Meng's invasion of 219-220. Wu's 238 outline (1.4 million km²) is used from 220, and the Han rows of 220-223 (shown as Shu Han from 221) take Shu Han's 224 outline, so the two do not overlap. Before 220 the data still gives Jiao, Changsha and Guiyang to the Han.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Lü Meng's invasion of Jing Province

patches.note: Khartoum fell to the Mahdi on 26 January 1885 and the Mahdist State held the Sudan until Omdurman (1898) and Umm Diwaykarat (1899); Suakin on the Red Sea and Wadi Halfa stayed Anglo-Egyptian. The border data has British Africa drawing Egypt and the whole Sudan as one piece in 1885-1889 (the corrections layer cuts the Sudan out of it, leaving the Sudan blank) and starts the Mahdist State in 1890. The Mahdist State's 1890 outline is used for 1885-1889, and British Africa takes its 1890 Egyptian piece (Egypt and the Suakin coast) in place of the Egypt-and-Sudan piece. Equatoria, where Emin Pasha held out until 1889, is drawn as Mahdist, as in the border data's 1890 outline.

Kuwait (a British-protected sheikhdom from the agreement of 23 January 1899 to 1961) is drawn as part of the Sultanate of Muscat and Oman in 1900-1921, and Qatar (a British protectorate under the treaty of 1916 until 1971) in 1916-1935; neither was ever Omani. Both pieces move to the British shape, the way the border data draws Kuwait from 1922, Qatar from 1936 and Bahrain throughout (Britain's Gulf protectorates; Correlates of War codes both as passing to the United Kingdom).

After the plebiscite of 20 March 1921 the Conference of Ambassadors divided Upper Silesia (20 October 1921). East Upper Silesia (about 3,214 km²: Katowice, Chorzów, Tarnowskie Góry, Lubliniec, Rybnik, Pszczyna) became part of Poland on 20 June 1922 as the Silesian Voivodeship; Bytom and Gliwice, at the south-eastern tip of German Silesia, stayed German. The border data keeps all of Upper Silesia German until 1944. The Polish part is cut out of Germany (as a hole along its edge) and added to Poland for 1922-1939, along a line traced from the towns on either side (west of Lubliniec, between Tarnowskie Góry and Bytom, round Bytom, between Zabrze and Ruda, south of Gliwice, west of Rybnik, to the Oder at the Olza) and the old Prussian-Austrian border in the south; it approximates the line at the border data's resolution (about 3,000 km²). The Polish part of Cieszyn Silesia, Polish from 1920, is still drawn German.

The Saar was governed by the League of Nations from 1920, with its coal mines given to France, until it voted to rejoin Germany (13 January 1935) and was returned on 1 March 1935. The border data draws it with France in 1920-1931 but inside Germany's 1932-1935 shape. For 1932-1934 the Saar as the border data draws it in 1930 is cut out of Germany and drawn with France again, as in the earlier years.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Territory of the Saar Basin

patches.note: The Treaty of London (19 April 1839) left the eastern third of Luxembourg as a grand duchy in personal union with the Netherlands, and the Treaty of London of 1867 confirmed its independence and neutrality; the union ended in 1890, when Wilhelmina became queen of the Netherlands and the grand duchy passed to the house of Nassau-Weilburg. Luxembourg was never Dutch territory, but the border data draws it inside the Netherlands from 1840 (and still in 1890-1916, under its own Luxembourg shape). It is drawn as Luxembourg from 1840 with its 1890 outline and taken out of the Netherlands' shape for 1840-1916.

British New Guinea was placed under the Commonwealth of Australia in 1902 and constituted as the Territory of Papua on 1 September 1906. Australian forces occupied German New Guinea in September 1914 (the German administration surrendered on 17 September) and Australia held it under a League of Nations mandate from 17 December 1920 as the Territory of New Guinea (the mainland, New Britain, New Ireland, the Admiralty Islands and Bougainville). The border data files Papua under the British Colonial Empire from 1906, and both territories from 1915 to 1945. They move to Australia for 1906-1914 (Papua) and 1915-1942 (both). In 1943-1945 the border data already draws much of them as Australian beside the British pieces and the Japanese occupation; those wartime years are left as they are. For 1946-1974 see the corrections layer (Papua New Guinea).

The British military administration of the former Italian Somaliland ended on 1 April 1950, when Italy took it over as the UN Trust Territory of Somaliland until it joined British Somaliland as the Somali Republic on 1 July 1960. The border data keeps it inside British Africa's East African piece until 1959. For 1950-1959 it is cut out of British Africa (as a hole along the land border the border data draws for Italian Somaliland in 1935 and British Africa's own coastline) and drawn as Italian-administered (Italian Africa).
